# ataila_permission_catalog (Data Source)

Every fine-grained permission key the platform honours, `<feature>-<level>-<scope>`. The roles catalogue also holds role names that are not permission keys (`user`, `admin`, …).

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "ataila_permission_catalog" "users" {
  feature = "users"
}

output "grantable_user_keys" {
  value = [for p in data.ataila_permission_catalog.users.permissions : p.key if p.grantable]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `feature` (String) Only this feature's keys, for example `users`.

### Read-Only

- `permissions` (Attributes List) The keys, ordered by key. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permissions))

<a id="nestedatt--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `permissions`

Read-Only:

- `category` (String) The group the portal shows it in.
- `description` (String) What the key allows.
- `feature` (String) The feature it belongs to.
- `grantable` (Boolean) May be granted to a person (`ataila_user_role_grant`). A key that is not grantable is still honoured for those who hold it.
- `key` (String) The permission key, for example `users-read-global`.
- `label` (String) Display name.
- `level` (String) `read` or `admin`.
- `mintable` (Boolean) May be carried by an API token.
- `scope` (String) `global` or `tenant`.
